title: editor: hide mouse cursor while typing
body:
Adds an opt-in `editor.hideMouseCursorOnTyping` setting (default `false`) that hides the mouse
pointer after keyboard text input in the editor and reveals it again on the next pointer or focus
activity.

**Hiding** is driven from the semantic text input path (`_type`), not from raw key events, so
navigation keys, modifiers, paste, and programmatic edits leave the pointer alone.

**Revealing** happens on pointer move (guarded so that a re-render under a resting pointer does not
count as movement), pointer leave of the editor container, pointer down, wheel, context menu, editor
blur, and owner-window blur. The state is also cleared when the setting is turned off, when the model
is replaced, and when the editor is disposed.

**IME composition deliberately keeps the pointer visible.** Composition candidate windows are
positioned relative to the pointer on several platforms, and hiding it mid-composition makes the
candidate window hard to track, so `_startComposition` reveals the pointer and `_compositionType`
keeps it revealed for the duration of the composition.

Scope is the editor only. The integrated terminal and the rest of the workbench are unaffected — see
the follow-ups below.

The Monaco editor API declarations (`monaco.d.ts`, `standaloneEnums.ts`) are regenerated, and the
diff editor gets a targeted CSS override because its pre-existing `!important` resize cursors would
otherwise beat the `cursor: none` rule.

Fixes #29351

## Follow-ups

Deliberately out of scope for this PR:

- **Integrated terminal.** The terminal draws its own cursor and does not go through
  `CodeEditorWidget`, so it needs a separate hook; the setting description says so explicitly.
- **Shared overflow widget containers.** Suggest/hover widgets rendered into a workbench-level
  overflow container live outside the editor's DOM subtree, so the `cursor: none` class does not
  reach them. Handling that means either hiding at a shared ancestor or propagating the state, both
  of which affect non-editor UI.
- **Chromium `kHideCursorWhileTyping`.** Chromium can do this natively at the compositor level.
  Once Electron ships a version exposing it, this implementation could delegate instead of managing
  the class in JS.

## Testing

- `node build/next/index.ts transpile`
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p src/tsconfig.json`
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/editor/browser/widget/codeEditor/codeEditorWidget.ts src/vs/editor/common/config/editorOptions.ts src/vs/editor/test/browser/widget/codeEditorWidget.test.ts`
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/editor/browser/widget/codeEditor/editor.css src/vs/editor/browser/widget/diffEditor/style.css`
- `npm run test-browser -- --browser chromium --run src/vs/editor/test/browser/widget/codeEditorWidget.test.ts`

The browser tests cover: default-off, hiding on text input, key events and paste *not* hiding, each
reveal source, the no-movement and descendant-`pointerleave` guards, IME (including cancelled and
interrupted compositions), config change, model replacement, disposal, and the computed
`cursor: none` on the editor and its descendants.

title: Auto mode repeatedly routes to a model (shown as "MAI-Code-1.1-Flash") that rejects the tool_search tool, causing hard 400 failures
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not installed as a separate extension — Copilot Chat is built into VS Code core in this version (confirmed via `code --list-extensions`: neither `GitHub.copilot` nor `GitHub.copilot-chat` are listed).
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0 (commit 110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419, x64)
- OS Version: macOS 15.7.7 (build 24G720)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent mode
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Model picker set to "Auto"; UI displayed the resolved model as "MAI-Code-1.1-Flash", but the backend error response identifies the model as "gpt-5"
- Logs:

Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.

Client Request Id: a29a0d77-c3e3-4fa2-9dba-92e3d4f963d7
GH Request Id: D43F:26678A:198B106:1D1BBD0:6A8C17D1
Reason: Request Failed: 400 {"error":{"message":"Tool 'tool_search' is not supported with gpt-5.","code":"invalid_request_body"}}

Frequency: This is not a one-off — I have hit this same failure mode multiple times before in Auto mode when the UI shows "MAI-Code-1.1-Flash" as the selected model. I was not able to capture Client/GH Request Ids for those earlier occurrences at the time. I also searched my own session history (both local session log and cloud-synced session store, up to a 180-day window) for the exact error text to attach more instances to this report, but found none — this class of hard client-side request failure does not appear to get persisted in the session/telemetry store, likely because the request never completes far enough to log a normal turn. The one occurrence documented above is the only one with verifiable IDs; the recurrence itself is a user report, not something I can independently substantiate with additional stored evidence.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open the Chat panel in Agent mode and set the model picker to "Auto".
2. Send a prompt that causes the agent to need a tool that is registered as a "deferred" tool (i.e. one that requires an initial `tool_search` call to discover/load before it can be invoked).
3. Auto mode selects/routes the request to a backend model surfaced internally as "gpt-5" (while the UI still shows a different model name, "MAI-Code-1.1-Flash"). This has recurred across multiple separate sessions for me, always when "MAI-Code-1.1-Flash" is the model Auto resolves to.
4. The request fails immediately with a 400 error because that backend model does not support the `tool_search` tool that the client included in the request's tool list.
5. There is no automatic fallback or retry on a different, compatible model — the whole turn fails outright and the user must manually retry (sometimes succeeding only after the model picker resolves to a different underlying model on retry).

Expected behavior: either "Auto" mode should not route tool-enabled requests to a model/backend that doesn't support the declared tools, or the client should omit unsupported tools (like `tool_search`) from the request when targeting a model known not to support them, with a graceful fallback instead of a hard failure. Given this appears to recur specifically around the "MAI-Code-1.1-Flash" routing target, it would help if the client logged/persisted these hard-failure banners so recurrence can be tracked with request IDs in the future.

title: chat: don't prompt for workspace trust on internal agent-session folders
body:
Fixes #332249

## Problem

The send-time workspace-trust gate added for agent-host chat treated two **internal** folders as user workspaces and prompted _"Do you trust the authors of the files in this folder?"_:

1. **Workspace-less quick chats** — the agent host runs them in an internal scratch dir `~/.copilot/chats/<id>`, which is persisted as the session's working directory. The gate read `workingDirectories` but ignored the `workspaceless` marker, so it prompted for the scratch dir.
2. **Worktree sessions** — VS Code creates isolated worktrees in a **sibling** `<repo>.worktrees/<name>` dir. Workspace-trust inheritance is equal-or-descendant only, so trusting `/repo` does not cover `/repo.worktrees/x`; opening such a session from the list (and a follow-up send) prompted even though the base repo is trusted.

Regression from #331895 / #331981.

## Fix

- **Quick chats:** `AgentHostSessionHandler._resolveSessionTrustFolders` now reads the session state once and, when `readSessionWorkspaceless(state._meta)` is set, returns a sentinel so `_invokeAgent` **skips the folder-trust gate** entirely — the scratch dir is an implementation detail, not a user workspace.
- **Worktrees:** trust is **inherited from the already-trusted base repository** before the gates run:
  - `SessionsService.canOpenSession` calls a shared `ensureSessionWorktreesTrusted` helper (open gate).
  - The handler's send gate applies the equivalent inheritance (covers follow-up turns, which bypass the sessions open gate — the handler is the only universal chokepoint).
  - Both are guarded **structurally** to `getWorktreesRoot(<repo>)`: bare `workTreeUri` does not prove VS Code created the worktree, so a working directory outside `<repo>.worktrees` can never inherit trust just because its reported base repo is trusted (addresses the [#331981 review note](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331981#discussion_r3831310974)).
- Extracts `getWorktreesRoot` into `platform/agentHost/common/worktreePaths.ts` so the node agent host and the browser trust gates share one implementation.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean; `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- Browser unit tests: `workspaceFolderManagement` (8) and agent-host `workspace trust` suite (10, incl. 5 new: quick-chat skip, worktree grant + follow-up turn, untrusted-repo prompt, structural-guard rejection, worktree-pending window).
- Full node unit suite: 15198 passing, 0 failing.

## Manual testing

- **Quick chat:** clear trust → Agents Window → "New Quick Chat" → send → no trust dialog (previously prompted for `~/.copilot/chats/<id>`). Control: "New Session" on an untrusted folder still prompts.
- **Worktree:** trust only a base repo → "New Session" on it with Worktree isolation → send (creates `<repo>.worktrees/<name>`) → reload → open from list and send a follow-up → no prompt. Control: with the base repo untrusted, it still prompts.

## Notes

- Branch is based on `release/1.135` (the regression ships in 1.135), so this PR targets `release/1.135`.
- Deferred follow-ups: validating creation provenance via `WORKTREE_META_REPOSITORY_ROOT` (stronger than the structural guard), and worktree-trust lifecycle/revocation (pre-existing; `setUrisTrust` is never revoked on worktree deletion).

title: Add table of contents with persistent visibility & code block language labels
body:
#332300 

This PR introduces two new features to the Markdown preview:

Table of Contents (TOC) — A navigable sidebar showing document headings with auto-scroll sync
Code Block Language Labels — Language badges (e.g., php, javascript, python) displayed on fenced code blocks
Both features are brand new and did not exist previously.

---

#### Features
1. Table of Contents

UI/UX:
- Collapsible sidebar on the left of the preview
- Shows all headings (h1–h6) with indentation by level
- Active heading highlighted based on scroll position
- Resizable width (drag handle), persisted in localStorage
- Toolbar toggle button with checkbox (synced to context key markdown.tocVisible)
- Persistence:
  - Visibility preference stored in extension globalState (markdown.preview.tocVisible)
  - Survives: tab close, VS Code restart, preview reopen
  - Default: visible (true)
Auto-scroll behavior:
- During document scroll: TOC panel scrolls minimally to keep active entry visible (with 4px edge gap)
- Manual click on TOC entry: Does not trigger TOC panel scroll — user stays at clicked position
- First/last headings can now reach true top/bottom of panel (no visual gap)

2. Code Block Language Labels
- Language identifier from fenced code blocks (php, js, python, etc.) displayed as a badge in the top-right corner of the code block
- Uses the existing tokenization from the markdown renderer
- Styled with theme-aware colors (uses `--vscode-editorCodeBlockLabel-background/foreground`)

#### Technical Implementation

TOC Architecture

```
MarkdownPreviewManager (owns globalState)
    ├── #tocVisible: boolean (persisted)
    ├── createPreview() / revivePreview() → passes tocVisible
    └── #setActivePreview() → sets context key 'markdown.tocVisible'

StaticMarkdownPreview / DynamicMarkdownPreview
    └── getAdditionalState() → includes tocVisible

Webview (preview-src/index.ts)
    ├── Reads State.TocVisible from vscode.getState() / data-state
    ├── Calls buildTableOfContents()
    └── If TocVisible === false → toggleTableOfContents()

tableOfContents.ts (webview module)
    ├── Module-level tocVisible (synced from State)
    ├── skipScrollActiveEntry flag (prevents auto-scroll on manual click)
    ├── scrollActiveEntryIntoView() (minimal scroll with edge gap)
    └── Resize handle → persists width to localStorage
```

Language Labels
- Injected during markdown rendering via markdown-it plugin
- Added as <span class="code-block-language-label"> inside code block wrapper
- CSS uses design tokens for theming consistency

#### Test

##### Test Workspace
Open the test workspace file:

```
extensions/markdown-language-features/test-workspace/e.md
```

This file contains:
- Multiple heading levels (h1–h6) for TOC testing
- Fenced code blocks with various languages (php, javascript, python, typescript, etc.)
- Enough content to trigger scrolling

2. Open Markdown Preview (Ctrl+Shift+V / Cmd+Shift+V)
3. Verify TOC appears on the left with all headings
4. Scroll in the preview → verify active heading highlights in TOC

6. Scroll to first/last heading → verify TOC scrollbar reaches true top/bottom
7. Click toolbar toggle button → verify TOC hides/shows, checkbox matches
8. Close preview tab, reopen → verify TOC visibility persists
9. Restart VS Code → verify TOC visibility persists
10. Drag resize handle → verify width persists after reload

3. Switch themes (light/dark/high contrast) → verify badge colors adapt

title: chat: clear progress when session provider is disposed
body:
I generated this by scanning my logs, pls take if it's good/useful

---
🤖 

## Summary

- clear a chat session provider's in-progress entry synchronously when its item controller is disposed
- prevent an in-flight progress refresh from publishing after its controller has been removed or replaced
- add regression coverage for adding and removing provider progress across controller disposal

## Problem

Recent Code Insiders renderer logs repeatedly showed warnings while Agent Host-backed chat session providers were shutting down:

```text
2026-08-22 15:34:26.089 [warning] Attempted to report in-progress status for unknown chat session type 'copilotcli'
2026-08-22 15:34:26.282 [warning] Attempted to report in-progress status for unknown chat session type 'copilot-cloud-agent'
```

The warning was produced by the controller disposal path itself. `registerChatSessionItemController` removed the controller from `_itemControllers` and then called `updateInProgressStatus`. That asynchronous recomputation eventually called `reportInProgress`, which correctly noticed that the controller no longer existed and logged the warning. It also retained a zero-count entry for a provider that was no longer registered.

There was a related race for progress updates already in flight: a refresh could start while a controller was registered, await item resolution, and publish after that controller had been disposed or replaced.

## Fix

Controller disposal now deletes the corresponding progress entry directly and emits `onDidChangeInProgress` only when an entry was actually removed. This keeps controller registration and its derived progress state within the same lifecycle instead of querying a provider after teardown.

`updateInProgressStatus` also captures the current controller identity before awaiting item resolution and verifies that the same controller is still registered before publishing. This prevents stale work from restoring progress for a disposed or replaced provider.

Active providers retain the existing progress computation behavior.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatSessions/chatSessions.contribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatSessions/chatSessionsService.test.ts`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatSessions/chatSessionsService.test.ts --grep "removes in-progress state when its controller is disposed"`
- pre-commit hygiene checks

The focused regression test passes and verifies that an in-progress entry is published while the controller is registered and removed when its registration is disposed.

title: Prevent stale Claude queries from consuming prompts after rebind
body:
## Summary

- retire the previous Claude prompt iterator when a `Query` is rebound, so it cannot consume the fresh query's first prompt
- stop messages from a stale `Query` before they reach the router or settle the shared prompt queue
- cover both races with deterministic queue and pipeline regressions

## Problem

The Claude pipeline keeps one prompt queue across SDK `Query` rebinds. The previous query can remain alive briefly after the swap:

1. Its input loop can still be parked on the shared iterable. The SDK checks its abort signal only after pulling a prompt, so it can remove the new query's first prompt and then drop it.
2. Its output loop can still yield a buffered `result`. Without an ownership check, that result settles the new query's queue head and completes the turn without an assistant response.

In both cases the affected prompt appears to do nothing, while a subsequent prompt works normally.

title: Add worker-src to MCP app webview CSP (fixes #331633)
body:
Fixes #331633.

`_injectPreamble` in `chatMcpAppModel.ts` builds the MCP app webview CSP with `default-src`, `script-src`, `style-src`, `connect-src`, `img-src`, `font-src`, `media-src`, `frame-src`, `object-src` and `base-uri` — but no `worker-src`. Per CSP spec the browser then falls back to `script-src`, which carries no `blob:` scheme, so any MCP app that spawns a Web Worker from a `blob:` URL is blocked:

```
Creating a worker from 'blob:vscode-webview://…' violates the following Content
Security Policy directive: "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' <domains>".
Note that 'worker-src' was not explicitly set, so 'script-src' is used as a
fallback. The action has been blocked.
```

This breaks a class of MCP apps rather than a single case — anything using MapLibre/Mapbox GL JS (tile parsing), PDF.js, Monaco, or other blob-worker libraries. The failure is silent: the data layer renders, the basemap never paints, and nothing surfaces in the chat UI.

Not fixable from the MCP resource side, and no MCP Apps spec change needed — the reference host (`examples/basic-host/serve.ts` in `modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`) already sets `worker-src 'self' blob:` unconditionally. `modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps#566` (resource-level `workerDomains`) is an independent optional enhancement, not a prerequisite.

Verified against `main`: the directive is still absent.

title: agent host: self-heal Copilot client cold-start config-changed abort
body:
## What

When a startup-config value (session sync, SDK log level, enterprise host, system proxy, built-in GitHub MCP, …) changes **while the Copilot SDK client is starting**, `_ensureClient` aborts the now-stale start and throws `CopilotClientStartupConfigChangedError`. Because the *next* start uses the current config, that abort is transient — yet it was surfaced to session restore, producing sticky, user-visible failures such as **"Provider copilotcli could not describe … yet"** / **"Couldn't open session"**, even though the backend recovered moments later.

## Change

`_ensureClient` now transparently re-acquires the client **once** with the current config instead of propagating the transient abort:

- The existing acquisition body is extracted into `_ensureClientOnce()` — per-attempt coalescing via `_clientStarting` is unchanged.
- `_ensureClient()` wraps it in a bounded retry loop that retries **only** on `CopilotClientStartupConfigChangedError`, bounded by `MAX_STARTUP_CONFIG_RETRIES` (1).
- The acquire-and-retry sequence is shared across all concurrent callers via `_ensureClientHealing`, so the retry budget is **global** (a late caller cannot reset it and drive unbounded starts).
- Shutdown still short-circuits; every other startup failure propagates unchanged.

No caller observes the transient abort; a genuinely persistent config problem still gives up after the bound.

## Tests

`src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`:
- self-heals a clean config-changed cold-start abort and returns the catalog
- self-heals a clean config-changed cold-start abort on the restore describe path
- gives up after the bounded number of re-acquires when the startup config keeps changing
- shares one global re-acquire budget across concurrent client acquisitions
- coalesces concurrent client acquisitions across a single re-acquire
- (updated) self-heals a config-changed cold-start abort when stopping the started client fails

Full suite green (318 passing, 0 failing).

## Notes for reviewers

- This is the **provider-side** half only. The **host-side** readiness gap (`AgentService._restoreSessionState` throwing `-32603 "could not describe … yet"` without waiting for provider readiness) and the **client-side** sticky error-model reconciliation are tracked separately and intentionally **not** addressed here.
- Deliberately narrow and defensive.

Related to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8895

title: Avoid false listener leak warnings for many inputs
body:
## Summary

Avoid false-positive listener leak warnings when users have hundreds of open editor inputs and text models.

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Root cause, not disposal masking**: Recent Insiders renderer logs showed the same global readonly and custom-label events crossing the default 175-listener threshold while opening many documents. The listeners are tied to live editor inputs/models and correctly disposed; their high cardinality is intentional.
- **Keep leak detection active**: The per-emitter threshold is raised to 500 rather than disabled, matching existing editor/model events designed for hundreds of open inputs. Stable emitter names are added so any future warning identifies its source.
- **One issue only**: Older Agent Host `SessionDatabase has been disposed` failures were investigated but had already been fixed by #331759 and did not recur in newer logs, so this PR does not touch that code.
- **Likely owners**: There is no matching CODEOWNERS rule. File history points to @bpasero for files/editor infrastructure and @benibenj for custom editor labels.

</details>

## Changes

- Allow up to 500 listeners on `FilesConfigurationService._onDidChangeReadonly`.
- Allow up to 500 listeners on `CustomEditorLabelService._onDidChange`.
- Name both emitters for actionable leak diagnostics.

## Validation

- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/services/filesConfiguration/common/filesConfigurationService.ts src/vs/workbench/services/editor/common/customEditorLabelService.ts`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/filesConfiguration/test/browser/filesConfigurationService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/editor/test/browser/customEditorLabelService.test.ts` (15 passing)

title: Re-enable Kerberos proxy smoke test on GitHub Actions
body:
## Summary

Revert #332064, re-enable the Kerberos-authenticated macOS PAC proxy smoke test on GitHub Actions, and keep the Actions runner control plane outside the authenticated test proxy.

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions and evidence from the investigation:

- **Keep full coverage enabled**: All four Agents Window cases continue to run through the Kerberos-authenticated proxy.
- **Tests themselves pass**: Cancelled runs consistently report all four Kerberos tests passing before `The operation was canceled` appears during step completion.
- **Not a process-shutdown timeout**: Squid uses a one-second shutdown lifetime, and the script reaps Squid, the PAC server, and the KDC. Post-cancellation diagnostics show no surviving test processes.
- **The system PAC also affects the runner**: Cancelled-run Squid logs contain repeated unauthenticated 407 responses for `broker.actions.githubusercontent.com` and `run-actions-*.actions.githubusercontent.com` while the Kerberos PAC is active.
- **Likely cancellation mechanism**: If the Actions runner reconnects while its control-plane hosts are behind the authenticated PAC, the 407 responses can disrupt its job lease. The runner receives the cancellation after cleanup restores normal networking.
- **Maintain smoke-test isolation**: The PAC now routes `*.actions.githubusercontent.com` directly. The smoke-test process cannot use that route because its dedicated primary group remains blocked from non-loopback direct traffic by PF.

</details>

## Changes

- Restore the GitHub Actions Kerberos proxy smoke step removed by #332064.
- Return `DIRECT` from the Kerberos PAC for `*.actions.githubusercontent.com` so the runner control plane remains connected.

## Validation

- Verified the cancelled artifact contains 407 responses for both the Actions broker and run-service endpoints.
- Verified all four Kerberos smoke tests passed before cancellation.
- Verified the PAC maps Actions control-plane hosts to `DIRECT` and keeps `api.github.com` and `vscode-smoke.test` on the authenticated proxy.
- GitHub Actions YAML parsing, proxy harness shell syntax, and `git diff --check` pass.

title: Agents Window does not forward Copilot CLI experiment settings (chat.agentHost.copilot.*, chat.copilot.*) into the local agent host root config
body:
## Problem

`AgentHostCopilotCliSettingsContribution` is the only thing that forwards the Copilot CLI experiment settings from VS Code configuration into the local agent host's root config (`AgentHostRootConfigForwarder`). It is registered solely by the workbench:

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHost.contribution.ts:38`
  (imported via `src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts`)

The standalone Agents Window (`src/vs/sessions`) has its own local-agent-host contribution module and does **not** register it:

- `src/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.ts:247-255` imports `./contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/localAgentHost.contribution.js`
- `src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/localAgentHost.contribution.ts:89-94` registers `AgentHostContribution`, `AgentHostTerminalContribution`, `AgentHostAllowSignedOutWhenUsableContribution`, the notification contributions, and `LocalAgentHostContribution` — but not `AgentHostCopilotCliSettingsContribution`.

## Effect

In the Agents Window, toggling any of the following has no effect on the local agent host — the host stays at the schema default for each root-config key:

| Setting | Root-config key |
|---|---|
| `chat.agentHost.copilotSdk.logLevel` | `copilotSdkLogLevel` |
| `chat.agentHost.opus48Prompt.enabled` | `opus48Prompt` |
| `chat.agentHost.copilot.toolSearch.enabled` | `toolSearchEnabled` |
| `chat.agentHost.copilot.toolSearch.deferThreshold` | `toolSearchDeferThreshold` |
| `chat.agentHost.copilot.reasoningSummary.enabled` | `reasoningSummary` |
| `chat.agentHost.copilot.multiTurnContextRouting.enabled` | `multiTurnContextRouting` |
| `chat.copilot.subagentModelGuidance.enabled` (#332089) | `subagentModelGuidance` |
| `chat.agentHost.copilot.modelCapabilityOverrides` | `modelCapabilityOverrides` |

Notably `toolSearchEnabled` defaults to `true` in the schema, so tool search cannot be turned *off* from the Agents Window; the experiment-gated keys default to `false` and cannot be turned *on*.

`AgentHostTerminalContribution` (which forwards `enableCustomTerminalTool` via the same forwarder) *is* registered in the sessions path, so the forwarder machinery itself works there — only the Copilot CLI settings contribution is missing.

## Context

Surfaced during review of #332089. Not introduced by that PR — the gap predates it and applies to every key above.

`vscode.window.createWebviewPanel` lets extensions set a `title` and `iconPath` on the tab, but there is no way to set a tooltip on the tab label.

Our extension (Google Earth Engine) opens asset preview panels whose tab title is the short asset name (e.g. `my_image`). title: [Reference only] Launch skill: batched automation prototype
body:
## Reference / inspiration only

This draft collects the full launch-skill prototype developed during the performance investigation. It is **unlikely to land as-is**: the change is intentionally broad and should instead be mined for smaller, focused follow-ups. The main purpose is to preserve working examples and measurements for inspiration.

## Ideas demonstrated

- A one-process direct-CDP driver with JSON scenarios (`prepare`, checked `chat`, and `fork` actions).
- Aggressive but validated modal handling: known Workspace Trust dialogs are handled immediately, awaited until hidden, and unknown dialogs fail instead of allowing clicks behind them.
- Exact Monaco prompt insertion/read-back before Send is enabled and clicked.
- Adaptive response waiting that observes loading and completion instead of sleeping a fixed 30 seconds.
- Fast fork completion detection based on actual transcript/session state changes.
- Automatic workspace selection/reselection for transient Agents-window state.
- Privacy-aware action recording hints with redacted text and compact DOM mutation summaries.
- An isolated benchmark runner, scenario JSON format, raw result JSON, and an in-skill dashboard covering both Agents and Editor windows.

## Why it is useful as inspiration

The prototype is especially effective at the expensive inner loop: dismissing modals, sending chat messages, waiting for model replies, and validating fork completion without additional model turns or separate Playwright processes for every action. Those techniques can be extracted into a general Playwright CLI batching approach or smaller reusable helpers.

Historical three-run results in the included dashboard reduced the two-turn/fork scenario from roughly 45–62 seconds and 21–43 Playwright invocations to 14.87–15.37 seconds median with one automation process, with 3/3 passes on both surfaces and ~0.22–0.24 second median fork detection.

Fresh validation after rebasing onto current `main`:

| Surface | Result | Launch | Full scenario | Fork | Visible modals after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Agents | Pass | 1.17 s | 20.04 s | 0.27 s | 0 |
| Editor | Pass | 0.72 s | 15.30 s | 0.23 s | 0 |

Both fresh runs used unique non-git fixture folders, handled Workspace Trust where needed, verified both model replies, left the repository worktree list unchanged, and cleaned the launched profiles.

## Scope warning

This includes the benchmark runner, dashboard, raw JSON results, scenario format, driver, modal gate, chat/fork recipes, and recorder in one reference PR. Reviewers should treat it as a design/prototyping artifact and source of smaller optimizations, not as a request to approve the entire architecture unchanged.

The Copilot SDK can publish `session.idle` before its on-disk event journal becomes visible. During that window, `session.rpc.debug.collectLogs` succeeds but returns `events.jsonl` in `skippedEntries` with reason `not found`.

Agent Host did not inspect that result and always reported provider logs as included, even when the SDK staged no provider entries.

## Fix

- Retry Copilot debug collection only while `events.jsonl` is temporarily skipped as `not found`.
- Bound retries to 50 attempts with a 20 ms delay (about one second maximum).
- Clean up SDK fallback directories between retry attempts.
- Return and propagate whether the SDK actually collected provider entries so `providerLogsIncluded` reflects the archive contents.
- Avoid retrying permanent skip reasons.

## Tests

- Added unit coverage for successful collection, the transient journal race, intermediate-directory cleanup, and permanent skips.
- Added a recorded Copilot Agent Host E2E regression that materializes a session, completes a turn, exports its debug logs, and verifies that the manifest contains a provider-specific entry.
- Focused E2E replay passed 5 consecutive runs.

title: fix: keep hover color picker open while mouse is over the color decorator (#331433)
body:
## Description

Fixes #331433.

### Problem
When hovering a color swatch (e.g. `color: white` in CSS), the hover color picker is easily dismissed by a tiny mouse movement while the pointer is still over the color decorator (the injected swatch).

The keep-open logic in `ContentHoverController._shouldKeepCurrentHover` only keeps the hover alive when the mouse is **inside** the hover/picker widget's DOM node (or while the mouse button is held). When the pointer remains on the swatch itself but moves a few pixels, the `showsOrWillShow` path can recompute a different anchor and hide the picker.

### Fix
Extend `isMouseOnColorPickerOrChoosingColor` so that, while the color picker is visible, the hover is also kept open when the mouse is over the color decorator (`isOnColorDecorator`). This mirrors the existing mouse-down behaviour in `_shouldKeepHoverWidgetVisible`, which already uses `isOnColorDecorator` to keep the hover visible while interacting with the swatch.

```ts
const isMouseOnColorDecorator = isColorPickerVisible && isOnColorDecorator(mouseEvent);
return isMouseOnHoverWithColorPicker || isMaybeChoosingColor || isMouseOnColorDecorator;
```

### How to test
1. Open a `.css` file and write `color: white;` (color decorators on hover).
2. Hover the white swatch so the color picker appears.
3. Move the mouse slightly while remaining over the swatch — the picker should stay open.
4. Move the mouse onto the picker — it should remain open.
5. Move the mouse off the swatch/picker — the hover should dismiss as before.

Optionally run the editor hover/color picker test suites:
`yarn test --grep "Content Hover"` (or the color picker standalone tests).

title: Persist session archiving without restoring the session
body:
## The bug

Archiving a session in the Agents window could appear to succeed — the session vanished from the list — while recording nothing, so it reappeared after a refresh or restart. This hit hardest on old sessions whose working directories or worktrees no longer exist.

## Root cause

When a client dispatched `session/isArchivedChanged` for a session with no live host state, `AgentService.dispatchAction` first `await`ed `restoreSession(...)`. Restore reopens the session's working directory, and for a missing one **only an *already* archived session resumes read-only** — otherwise it tries to recreate the worktree and throws.

That is circular: archiving is precisely what would have made it archived. The operation was impossible for exactly the sessions that needed it most. The failed restore rejected the action, nothing was persisted, and the client never rolled back.

## The fix

Archived/read toggles are now applied **without materializing the session**: the flag is written to the session database and the catalogue delta is published via `root/sessionSummaryChanged`. The envelope and its side effects — worktree cleanup on archive, `onArchivedChanged`, Agent Merge sync — still run, since none of them need live state.

### Further bugs found and fixed along the way

- **`SessionSummaryNotifier` could not publish for an un-loaded session.** It re-derives summaries from live state and bails when there is none, so AHP-specified catalogue mutations were silently dropped. It now supports pushing changes into an announced summary, keeping a single notification path.
- **`removeSession` cleared the announced summary** — but it is also the idle-eviction hook, and eviction emits no `sessionRemoved`, so clients keep listing the session. A session that was opened and later evicted therefore looked *unknown*, and archiving it was dropped entirely. This is likely the most common archive flow (open a session, navigate away, archive later). The baseline now outlives eviction; `deleteSession` clears it explicitly.
- **The passive route was chosen from a stale snapshot.** `requiresSessionRestore` is computed at dispatch entry, but the callback runs behind earlier queued dispatches — so a toggle was dropped outright if an earlier action restored the session meanwhile. Residency is now re-checked at execution time, joining any in-flight restore.
- **The Agents window applied rejected envelopes.** It ignored `rejectionReason`, contradicting AHP reconciliation (a rejected action's optimistic effect must be reverted). It also flipped the archived observable with no connection to persist through.

## Protocol conformance

Dispatching a session action while *not subscribed* to that session is explicitly supported by AHP:

> "A client therefore answers by dispatching the ordinary `chat/*` action **to that chat's channel** — it does **not** need to have subscribed to the chat first." — `docs/specification/session-channel.md`

`dispatchAction` is a fire-and-forget notification, so the client is not owed an acknowledgement, and convergence for such clients is specified to ride `root/sessionSummaryChanged`, which is broadcast to every client regardless of subscription. Since that channel documents `read/done state` as part of its payload, the previous behaviour was a **conformance gap** — we dropped a mutation the protocol says we must publish. No protocol change was needed.

Creating `agentSessionData/<id>` is how Agent Host claims a session away from the extension host's Copilot CLI list, so the passive path refuses to do it for a session the host has never surfaced, matching AHP's "silently ignore actions for non-existent sessions".

## Out of scope

Un-adopted legacy Copilot CLI sessions (`ehcliAdoptable`) continue to be dropped rather than persisted, since persisting them would claim ownership away from the extension host. Filed separately.

## Testing

Nine regression tests added, **each verified to fail without the fix and pass with it**:

- persists + publishes without restoring (archive and read)
- succeeds when the working directory is gone (the motivating case)
- succeeds for a session that was opened and then idle-evicted
- lands when an earlier queued action restored the session
- creates no session database for an unknown session
- `deleteSession` still clears the announced baseline
- a rejected envelope leaves the session unarchived

Full suites green: 5,584 agentHost + 2,464 sessions + 1,222 workbench agentSessions. `typecheck-client`, `eslint`, and `valid-layers-check` all clean.

(Written by Copilot)

External sessions are agent sessions created outside VS Code, such as in Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, Claude Code, or Codex. **Recent** shows up to the two most recently updated external sessions from the last seven days, and stops showing one after two newer local sessions have been started since its last update.

## Set up

- Start VS Code with a fresh profile.
- Create several agent sessions outside VS Code in applications available to you. Include Copilot CLI or the GitHub Copilot app, and Codex and/or Claude Code if you have them. Give the sessions a clear update order by sending messages at different times.

3. Select another external-session mode, restart VS Code, and verify the explicit selection is preserved in both session lists. Return the filter to **Recent**.

## Moving on from external sessions

1. Start with an external session visible under **Recent**, then create a local session after the external session's last update by sending its first message. Verify the external session remains visible.
2. Create a second local session after that same external update. Verify the currently visible external session does not abruptly disappear while you are using the list.
3. Switch the **External** filter away from **Recent** and back to refresh its cutoff. Verify an external session is now hidden when two local sessions were started after its last update, while newer external sessions remain eligible.
4. Update the hidden session again in its external application and verify it can return to the recent set, displacing an older external session when appropriate.

title: Float chat pills above the chat input
body:
## What

The sessions status pills sat inside the chat input part's layout, so the transcript ended where the pills began. This floats them above the input instead, so content renders and scrolls underneath.

The row lands in exactly the position it held in flow — verified in a headless browser against a replica of the production DOM: the row's rect is unchanged (`top 478, bottom 508, left 32, right 688`), the banner and composer don't move, and the list grows by exactly 34px (the 30px row plus the input part's 4px flex gap).

## How

New opt-in `IChatWidgetViewOptions.persistentContentHeight`. Setting it:

- floats whatever the host mounts into `ChatInputPart.persistentContentContainerElement`
- reserves the same space below the transcript via the list's existing `paddingBottom`
- keeps the scroll-to-bottom button, the input scrim and the suggest-next widget clear of the floating content

Only the Agents window sets it (`SESSION_CHAT_INPUT_TOOLBAR_HEIGHT`, the row's rendered height). Every other chat widget keeps the previous in-flow `display: contents` layout — the float and the space reservation are one switch, so a host can't get half of it.

The row itself is click-through so the transcript stays interactive behind it. Its pills take hit-testing back and now paint an opaque background: `chat.list.background` as the base, with the (translucent) secondary button color composited on top via `background-image` — the same technique `.chat-scroll-down` already uses. Verified a 10%-alpha pill over a red backdrop renders `rgb(53,53,53)`, fully opaque.

`ChatListWidget.scrollToEnd()` now scrolls through the new padding. `reveal` stops at the last item's edge, so without it the list would never report being at the bottom and both auto-scroll-while-streaming and the scroll-down button would break.

## Trade-offs

- Right-clicking the empty space beside the pills no longer opens the visibility menu; right-clicking a pill still does. The deliberate 12px `.empty` strip that existed for that purpose is removed, since a click-through row can't be hit.
- The pills row's scrollbar slider can't be dragged for the same reason. It still shows the scroll position, and wheeling over a pill scrolls the row.
- The reserved space is a static constant, so it's held even while the row is hidden.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` clean
- `SessionChatPills` and `ChatTurnPills` unit suites pass
- All 26 `SessionChatPills_*` component fixtures render without errors
- Opt-out path re-verified live on a plain chat widget: `display: contents`, `position: static`, `pointer-events: auto`, scroll-down at `7px` — identical to before

The sessions pills screenshot baselines shift and need refreshing from CI.

title: Launch skill: Poll CDP readiness more frequently
body:
Reduce Code OSS launch latency by polling renderer CDP readiness every 100 ms instead of every second.

A small shared Node helper enforces the existing monotonic 90-second deadline, detects early launcher exit, and reports measured readiness time consistently across Bash and PowerShell.

In local validation, total launch-to-CDP time improved from a 1.78–2.02 s baseline to 1.01 s for Editor and 1.40 s for Agents; readiness itself was detected after 443 ms and 589 ms respectively.

Validated with direct success, timeout, dead-process, and slow-header checks, plus local Agents and Editor launches.
